summary.headline: Marketing and Sales mean different things by 'qualified' — an AI router would mis-route leads until you reconcile it.
summary.narrative: Across the team outputs there is one governed term in dispute and five core terms with no single owner. Marketing treats a lead as MQL on score-or-download alone; Sales only calls a deal 'Qualified' once budget and an economic buyer are confirmed. Until these are reconciled into one canonical glossary, any AI that routes leads or triggers a handoff will disagree with itself across teams. The recommended fix separates 'MQL' (a marketing interest signal) from 'Qualified' (a sales-accepted state) with one explicit transition rule.

positions.definition: MQL = lead score above threshold OR content download, regardless of budget/authority.
Qualified = budget confirmed AND economic buyer identified.

conflicts.impact: An AI router fed both definitions would mark a lead 'qualified' on a content download and hand it to a closing rep, while Sales' own rule rejects it for missing budget/authority — so the agent mis-routes leads and the two teams disagree on every handoff it triggers.
conflicts.recommended_canonical: Keep 'MQL' as a marketing interest signal (score above threshold OR high-intent content action). Reserve 'Qualified' (SQL) for a sales-accepted state requiring confirmed budget AND an identified economic buyer. Transition rule: an MQL becomes Qualified only after a human or agent verifies budget + economic buyer; the AI router uses 'Qualified' — never 'MQL' — as the handoff gate.

definitions.definition: A lead showing marketing-stage interest: lead score above the agreed threshold OR a high-intent content action (e.g. demo request, pricing-page download). An interest signal only — not a commitment of budget or authority.
A sales-accepted (SQL) state: confirmed budget AND an identified economic buyer. The single gate an AI router uses for handoff to a closing rep.
An account with at least one closed-won opportunity and an active paid subscription. Distinct from a free-trial or prospect account.
definitions.derived_from: No team currently owns this term — proposed canonical pending ownership assignment.

definitions.definition: The sum of open opportunities in a sales-accepted stage (post-Qualified) weighted at their stage probability. Excludes MQL-stage interest that has not converted to an opportunity.
A previously active paying Customer whose paid subscription has lapsed or been cancelled and not renewed within the grace window. Measured on the subscription, not the contact.

definitions.definition: Annual Recurring Revenue: the annualized value of active recurring subscriptions as of the measurement date, excluding one-time fees and non-recurring services.
